A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining experiments, downstream benchmark results, URL-component ablations and representation-probing analyses in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–2 and the supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same 1.5B, 16-layer Llama model, metadata prepending/appending procedures, loss masking and five learnable meta tokens. No algorithmic or architectural revision is introduced.

E1.justification: Both retain FineWeb-Edu pretraining, the same nine downstream benchmarks, quality/topic probing, Guardian authorship prediction and synthetic-document attention tests. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same standard-training and empty-metadata controls, metadata variants and URL-component comparisons. Appendix B.4 retains the Qwen2.5 1.5B and 7B probing comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3 retains the same training settings, probing sample sizes, splits and procedures. Removing Table 1's five-shot label changes documentation; no replacement shot count or changed evaluation procedure is reported.

E4.justification: The URL ablations, metadata-combination experiments, attention analyses, granularity probes and Qwen sanity checks are retained. The attention-entropy analysis in v2 Figure 6 already appeared in v1 Figure 13 and Appendix B.2.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averaging over three random seeds for configurations outperforming standard training. The layer-6 probing figure retains three-seed results and standard-deviation bars (v1 Figure 9; v2 Figure 10).

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–2 and the plotted results, including appendix figures, are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains averages of 46.7 for standard training and 47.7 for URL prepending. Revised captions summarize findings already available in v1.

T1.justification: Metadata definitions, quality-score discretization and entropy/distance calculations are retained. Neither version adds new formal assumptions, theoretical results or proofs relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list are unchanged, and the conclusion retains the same scope. Claims about fine-grained metadata, metadata appending, learnable meta tokens and representation probing are neither expanded nor narrowed.

C2.justification: The copying-effect explanation added to Section 4.3 already appears in v1 Section 4.1 and Appendix B.2. Revised probing prose restates the existing interpretation; uncertainty about mechanisms and post-training applicability remains.

D1.justification: Figure 4 now explicitly states that probing inference uses empty metadata, <boc><eoc>, and a new acknowledgment identifies CSCS/Alps support. Conversely, Table 1 drops its explicit five-shot description. The main implementation settings and Appendix C generation prompt are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Fan et al. (2025) is updated from a preprint reference to its NeurIPS publication, a bibliographic update rather than a new work or changed positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and punctuation edits, rewrites the Section 4.1 probing explanation, repeats the copying explanation in Section 4.3, and adds acknowledgments and publication headers. The main section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The existing attention-entropy figure moves from Appendix B.2 to the main text as Figure 6. Several captions are expanded, figures are repositioned or resized, and the layer-6 probing plot moves above its discussion. Both versions retain the same 15 figures and two tables.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves accessibility through more informative captions, placing the attention-entropy evidence beside the main argument, and explicitly documenting empty-metadata probing. These gains are tempered by deleting Table 1's five-shot specification, which weakens reproducibility documentation. The scientific evidence and unresolved mechanistic limitations remain unchanged.
